title: Review MediShield Life's Claim Limits to Address Gaps
what_it_is: Review MediShield Life's Claim Limits to Address Gaps

sections.label: MediShield Life coverage questions
sections.summary: Questions ask the Minister for Health about MediShield Life's role, claim limits, coverage adequacy, and pegging of hospital charges for complex procedures.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health in light of the recent case of MediShield Life disbursing only $4.50 as payout for an eye operation (a) whether he can reiterate the role of MediShield Life in our public healthcare financing system; (b) how does the Ministry determine the claim limits and ensure that MediShield Life provides adequate coverage for Singaporeans; and (c) whether the Ministry will review MediShield Life's claim limits to address the gaps.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health how does the Ministry ensure that the pegging of hospital charges for complex medical procedures for the purpose of assessing MediShield Life coverage is made current so that subsidised patients who undergo complex medical procedures will continue to be protected against large hospital bills.

sections.label: MediFund assistance amount
sections.summary: Last year, MediFund provided about $150 million in assistance to patients needing additional help with their bills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Last year, MediFund provided about $150 million in assistance to patients who require additional help with their bills.

sections.label: MediShield Life claims in 2017
sections.summary: In 2017, 555,000 MediShield Life claims were approved and $845 million was paid out.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: To provide members with a sense of the comparison, in 2017, 555,000 MediShield Life claims were approved and $845 million was paid out.

sections.label: Subsidised bills within claim limits
sections.summary: Latest figures show eight in 10 subsidised bills remain fully within the MediShield Life claim limits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The latest available figures show that eight in 10 subsidised bills remain fully within the MediShield Life claim limits.

sections.label: Government subsidy and claim limit
sections.summary: The Government subsidises approximately $7,500, leaving a balance of $4,500, about $1,400 above the MediShield Life claim limit in this case.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Of this amount, the Government subsidises approximately $7,500, leaving a balance of $4,500, or about $1,400 above the MediShield Life claim limit in this case.

sections.label: SNEC scaling down fees
sections.summary: Following the review, SNEC decided to scale down its fees for this procedure and other complex procedures with higher fees from 1 March 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Following the review, SNEC has decided to scale down its fees for this procedure and a number of other complex procedures with higher fees, and will do so from 1 March 2019.

sections.label: MediShield Life premium review timing
sections.summary: The review is being done under a commitment to keep premiums constant for five years after the 2015 introduction, with completion expected by end 2020 and future reviews about every three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: This review is also being done in the context of the commitment to keep premiums constant for five years after the scheme was introduced in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We expect the latest review to be completed by end 2020, but if the review is completed ahead of time, we will, of course, announce the revisions earlier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Moving forward, MOH intends to conduct these reviews of claim limits more regularly, around once every three years.

sections.label: Efforts to keep costs sustainable
sections.summary: Examples of efforts to keep costs sustainable include group procurement, technology for productivity, and healthcare technology assessments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Some examples of our efforts to keep costs sustainable are the use of group procurement to get better prices, tapping on technology to improve productivity and applying healthcare technology assessments to guide the appropriate use of services, devices and drugs.

sections.label: Three-year review objective parity
sections.summary: Whether five or three years, the objective is parity and rising in tandem, so it was decided to do it at three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Whether it is five years or three years, the objective is the same – to ensure that there is parity and that it rises in tandem, so we have decided to do it at three years.

sections.label: Three-year review timing aim
sections.summary: In terms of timing, three years is the aim for both reviews being done now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In terms of timing, three years is what we aim for, both the reviews that we are doing now.

sections.label: Deductibles for affordable premiums
sections.summary: Deductibles are necessary because they are one component of ensuring that premiums remain affordable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Deductibles are necessary, because they are one component of ensuring that the premiums remain affordable.

sections.label: MediShield Life review reserve transparency
sections.summary: A line item shows MediShield Life contributing zero dollars because it is within the deductible limit, and the question is whether the MOH review aligns with the spirit of the MediShield Life Review Committee report on greater transparency on reserve requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: He sees a line item "MediShield Life" contributing zero dollars, that is, because it is within the deductible limit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, my question really is about the review that MOH is undertaking – whether it is in line with the spirit of the MediShield Life Review Committee report, to have greater transparency on reserve requirements.

sections.label: SNEC review and implementation
sections.summary: The review's subject is what SNEC has reviewed and will implement from 1 March.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: It is, in fact, the subject of the review that we will do as well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And particularly in the context of this case, that is what SNEC has reviewed and will implement from 1 March.

sections.label: Adequacy ratio benchmarking
sections.summary: The adequacy ratio is not necessarily compulsorily or fixedly benchmarked against other jurisdictions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The adequacy ratio is not necessarily compulsorily or in a fix fashion benchmarked against other jurisdictions.

sections.label: Bills outside last 10%
sections.summary: Bills outside the last 10% are largely complex cases, with no age breakdown, and many patients fail the means test.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: On the second question, the bills that fall outside the last 10%, as I explained in my speech earlier, they are largely made up of complex cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I do not have the age breakdown for those cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: But, also, a sizeable component of those would be made up of patients who do not pass the means test for subsidies and that is why the amount outside of that would be larger.
